Data Types

　In TJS2, variables do not have "types", but values have types internally. Rather than saying they do not have types, it means that types are handled automatically/dynamically.
　Internal types include void, integer, real number, string, object, and octet sequence types.

void

　void represents that it represents nothing (the meaning is different from JavaScript). Newly declared variables are void.
　To compare void values with each other, use the === (identity) operator.
　The typeof operator returns "void" for this.

Integer Type

　TJS2 can handle 64-bit precision integers as the integer type. Integers are usually treated as signed integers, but as the sole exception, the >>> operator treats the left-hand side as an unsigned integer.
　The typeof operator returns "Integer" for this.

Real Number Type

　TJS2 can handle 64-bit precision real numbers (double-precision real numbers) as the real number type.
　The typeof operator returns "Real" for this.

String Type

　TJS2 can handle null-terminated strings with no length limit. A null-terminated string means that strings are handled assuming they end at \0.
　The character encoding uses wide characters (usually UNICODE), but whether wide characters are 16-bit or 32-bit depends on the environment where TJS2 was compiled. For example, on Windows it is 16-bit, while on Solaris or Linux it is 32-bit.
　The typeof operator returns "String" for this.

Object Type

　The object type is a type that holds an object. In addition to objects allocated with the new operator, functions, classes, property objects, and so on are all of object type.
　The typeof operator returns "Object" for this.

　Unlike TJS or JavaScript, object types in TJS2 internally hold two pointers: a pointer to the object itself, and a pointer to the object that serves as the context in which it should be used, enabling the implementation of so-called closures. The operator that changes this context part is the incontextof operator.

Octet Sequence Type

　The octet sequence type is a type for handling 8-bit wide data sequences (octet sequences). It is a type mainly used to handle binary data.
　The typeof operator returns "Octet" for this.
